description: A single rendered table (no axes, spectra or micrographs) that compares five segmentation/analysis methods — MatSAM, SAM, Canny, OTSU and Watershed — on five polycrystalline microstructure datasets: PI-1, SS, HEA, PI-2 and LCS[11]. The table has three column groups: Dataset, Metric, and Method, with the five method names as sub-columns under "Method". Each dataset occupies three stacked rows for the metrics ARI, F1 and Recall; every cell prints a two-decimal value followed by a ± relative deviation in percent. Bold and underlined entries appear only in the ARI rows: MatSAM is bold in all five ARI cells (0.62, 0.56, 0.59, 0.75, 0.96), and the underlined second-best ARI is Canny 0.52 for PI-1 and SAM for SS, HEA, PI-2 and LCS[11] (0.54, 0.56, 0.69, 0.86). MatSAM also attains the top F1 and Recall on PI-2 (0.82 / 0.83) and LCS[11] (0.96 / 0.97), but has the lowest F1 on HEA (0.35 vs SAM 0.52) and lower Recall than SAM on PI-1 (0.71 vs 0.86), SS (0.59 vs 0.60) and HEA (0.24 vs 0.43). The table supports the claim that MatSAM yields the best ARI clustering agreement on all five datasets, most clearly on LCS[11].

observations.observation: The figure is one rendered comparison table with column headers Dataset, Metric, Method, and Method sub-columns MatSAM, SAM, Canny, OTSU, Watershed.
Five datasets are tabulated: PI-1, SS, HEA, PI-2 and LCS[11]; the LCS entry carries the bracketed reference marker [11].
Three metrics are reported per dataset — ARI, F1 and Recall — each cell giving a two-decimal value with a ± relative deviation in percent.
MatSAM's ARI cell is bold in every dataset row: 0.62 (PI-1), 0.56 (SS), 0.59 (HEA), 0.75 (PI-2) and 0.96 (LCS[11]).
The underlined ARI values, i.e. the second-best entries, are 0.52 for Canny on PI-1 and 0.54, 0.56, 0.69 and 0.86 for SAM on SS, HEA, PI-2 and LCS[11] respectively.
The caption states that for the primary metric (ARI) bold and underlined values indicate the best and second-best results respectively, which matches the bold/underline positions seen in the image.
Only the ARI rows carry bold or underlined values; the F1 and Recall rows contain no bold or underlined entries.
MatSAM has the highest F1 and Recall on PI-2 (F1 0.82, Recall 0.83) and on LCS[11] (F1 0.96, Recall 0.97).
HEA is the one dataset where MatSAM's F1 (0.35) is below SAM's (0.52), and MatSAM's HEA Recall (0.24) is the lowest value in that row versus SAM 0.43.
On PI-1 the Recall ordering reverses the ARI ordering: MatSAM has 0.71 while SAM and Canny both reach 0.86.
Watershed gives the lowest ARI of every dataset (0.44, 0.24, 0.29, 0.20, 0.54) except HEA, where OTSU 0.37 sits above Watershed 0.29; OTSU is lowest on PI-2 (0.19).
The printed uncertainties are relative percentages; the largest is ±14.3 % (Canny ARI and F1 on HEA) and the smallest ±0.5 % (SAM F1 on PI-1).
The caption asserts the comparison covers polycrystalline datasets segmented by MatSAM versus SAM, Canny, OTSU and Watershed.
LCS[11] shows the highest overall performance of the table, with MatSAM reaching ARI 0.96, F1 0.96 and Recall 0.97.

unreadable_items: Several ± uncertainty terms wrap onto a second line within their cells (e.g. SAM on PI-1, Canny on PI-1); values were read from the printed text but line-wrapping makes a few cells visually ambiguous, e.g. PI-1 SAM ARI '+0.8 %)'.
Whether the ± term in the MatSAM PI-1 ARI cell is itself part of the bold span is not fully resolvable at the supplied rendering.
